text:
[title] Speculative decoding
[body] A small draft model proposes gamma tokens
[body] The target model verifies them in one forward pass
[body] Rejection sampling keeps the output distribution exact

novice.takeaway: A faster small model guesses several tokens ahead, which the main model checks at once, speeding things up without changing the final output.
questions: What exactly does 'gamma tokens' mean here?
How does rejection sampling technically ensure accuracy?
How much speed improvement does this technique give?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe speculative decoding speeds up model output while keeping results accurate.

peer.takeaway: Speculative decoding speeds up generation by having a small draft model propose tokens that a larger target model verifies in one pass, without changing output distribution.
questions: What determines the value of gamma?
How much speedup does this technique give alone?
How does rejection sampling mechanically work here?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe speculative decoding is a valid, distribution-preserving way to speed up inference.

expert.takeaway: The slide gives the standard mechanics of speculative decoding: draft proposal, single-pass verification, and exact-distribution rejection sampling.
questions: What value of gamma was tuned for the 2.4x result?
How does draft acceptance rate interact with continuous batching here?
expert.inferred_claim: Understand speculative decoding as the second pillar enabling the claimed 2.4x goodput gain.

metrics.intent: Our serving system delivers 2.4x higher goodput at p99 latency by pairing PagedAttention-style KV-cache management with speculative decoding.
